text:
alex: Heads-up — I'm prototyping KV reuse across requests to reduce cold token costs. Question: what cache key and routing shape should we use for prefix caching + session stickiness to get best reuse without blowing memory?

priya: Nice. TL;DR: separate stateless prefix cache from sticky session cache. Stateless keys should be heavily canonicalized and truncated; sticky cache can include a session id.

javier: Agree. Some practical constraints from profiling: GPU KV memory fragmentation kills reuse if we store variable-length entries. We saw memory growth + 20% p95 latency regressions when fragmentation hits.

emily: Data point from last perf run (infra-bot posted):
```
infra-bot: perf.profile.kv_snapshot
- workload: chat-multiuser
- prefix_hit_rate: 12%
- avg_kv_entries_per_gpu: 182k
- mem_frag_ratio: 0.28
- p95_latency_ms: 120 -> 88 on prefix-warm
- observed_evictions: 7.2k/min (LRU)
```

alex: Good numbers. If we can push prefix hit rate to ~40% we probably cut token cost by ~30% and p95 by ~25%. Problem: prefix keys explode if we use raw tokens.

priya: Key design suggestion: hash over canonicalized prefix tokens + model_variant + prefix_length_bucket. Example: `key = sha1(norm(prefix))[:16] + ":" + model + ":" + variant + ":" + bucket`. Keep bucket small (e.g., 32/64/128 token bins) so we don't create too many keys.

javier: Also: avoid user_id in stateless key. Use session_id only for sticky caches. Sticky routing: route session to same worker/GPU for interactive sessions to keep KV GPU-resident — but that reduces batching effectiveness.

emily: From experiments: sticky routing for sessions with qps < 10 and avg-turns > 5 gives best ROI. For high-qps stateless calls, prefer shared prefix cache + cross-worker KV paging.

sam: On eviction & paging: current runtime uses global LRU per-GPU. Fragmentation spikes because entries are variable length and we do best-fit allocation. Two mitigations: 1) switch to fixed-size chunks (4KB slabs) for KV storage, 2) implement background compaction when load < 30%.

priya: Slab approach would reduce external fragmentation but increases internal fragmentation for small entries. We can adaptive-size slab classes (128B, 512B, 4KB, 32KB) to balance. Also add metadata-free chaining so large KV spans multiple slabs.

alex: How about reuse across requests for common system prompts/references? We could proactively prefetch prefix KV for known templates on warmup. That avoids cold misses.

javier: Yep — maintain a small "hot prefix" table per-model (LRU with explicit pins). Pin templates for product flows. Pinning reduces effective eviction pressure but must be bounded.

emily: Regarding cache key canonicalization: normalize whitespace, strip ephemeral tokens (timestamps, ids), lowercase where appropriate, and truncate to last N tokens (e.g., 256) before hashing. Also record prefix length in metadata so we can match shorter prefix to longer cached KV when appropriate.

sam: Performance regression note: a previous change that added per-request full-context hashes caused key cardinality to explode and forced frequent evictions. Don't use full-context hashes unless you bucket.

priya: Routing ideas: hybrid sticky buckets. Keep a sticky slot per worker (small number) that accepts sticky sessions; other requests go into global pool for batching. This gives best of both: KV locality for interactive flows + high batch efficiency for stateless calls.

javier: Also consider cache versioning: include model id + quantization profile + kernel_variant in the key. If we change kernels or quantization we need to invalidate incompatible KV entries. Example key suffix: `":v2-kq8"`

alex: Can someone sketch a minimal key formula we can test?

priya: Sure — start with this canonical string then sha1 it:
```
canon = f"model={model}|variant={variant}|bucket={token_bucket}|prefix={norm_prefix_trunc}"
key = sha1(canon)[:20]
```
Keep an optional `session=` field appended for sticky-cache entries only.
```
canon_sticky = canon + f"|session={session_id}"
```

sam: Eviction policy tweak: prefer evicting entries with low reuse score = hits / (1 + age_seconds/3600) and penalize pinned entries only after global pressure. Add a soft-TTL for prefixes (default 6 hours) we can tune.

emily: Small experiment suggestion: pick two models and run A/B: baseline vs. new key + hybrid routing. Measure prefix hit rate, p95, memory fragmentation, and evictions/min. 48h run should surface regressions.

alex: I'll set up the A/B. @infra-bot can you allocate a canary fleet with sticky routing enabled and slab allocator config?

infra-bot: canary created: fleet=kv-reuse-canary-03, sticky_slots=8, slab_classes=[128,512,4096,32768], compaction=on, ttl_default=6h.

javier: Follow-up: add a logging metric for key_cardinality_per_min and prefix_key_growth to catch cardinality explosions early. Also emit reuse_score histogram.

priya: One more thought — expose an API for customers to opt into sticky sessions for chat UIs, but default to stateless for webhooks. That keeps platform defaults safe.

alex: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll post the A/B config + expected dashboards once ready. :thumbsup: 

emily: Awesome. ping if you want extra tracing for compaction windows.

sam: I'll add a perf test driver that simulates short interactive sessions vs stateless bursts so we can tune sticky slot counts.

alex: Closing this thread; will update with results.
